transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (CTO - Riverbend), Maya Singh (VP Product), Evan Brooks (Security)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Quick product walkthrough focused on rate-limits, org vs project API keys, quotas and multi-tenant controls. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs hosted for latency predictability and data isolation. Security discussion around SOC2, KMS, and audit logs. Next steps: pricing, sandbox, POC benchmarks, security deep-dive.

Topics:
- Org/project keys and per-project quotas
- Rate limiting shapes: token, request, concurrency
- Routing and fallbacks for Dedicated vs hosted
- Security controls: SSO, KMS, audit logs
\Action items: See metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, sorry for slight delay, Priya and I are excited to walk through how Redwood handles rate limits, org and project keys, multi-tenant controls. quick intros?
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: Hey hi, Tom here, CTO at Riverbend. We run a multi-tenant API for claims processing and want to add LLM-powered summaries, low latency is a must.
[00:21] Maya Singh: Maya from Product, we'll own integration side.
[00:25] Evan Brooks: Evan, security infra. I'll have the deep questions later.
[00:30] Priya Patel: Great, thanks. Quick note — we'll demo Console and API flows, and then show Optimize suggestions around batching and quotas.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: To set context, Riverbend mentioned two big constraints: strict PII handling and need for predictable per-tenant quota control. Is that still accurate?
[00:45] Tom Alvarez: Yes, and also timeline — pilot in next 6 weeks, production Q1.
[00:51] Jordan Lee: Got it. We'll keep that timeline in mind.
[01:05] Priya Patel: Jumping into Console — first screen is Org level settings. You can create multiple projects under an org, each project gets its own project API key. We often see customers map a project to a service team or tenant.
[01:20] Priya Patel: (screen share noise) Here you can set per-project quotas: requests per minute, tokens per minute, monthly token cap. There's also a concurrency limit that prevents overloading Dedicated pools.
[01:32] Maya Singh: Is concurrency per-project or global?
[01:35] Priya Patel: You can do both — project-level concurrency and org-level guardrails. For example, org-level burst capacity ensures one project doesn't starve others.
[01:45] Tom Alvarez: How do you implement rate-limiting enforcement? Is it client-side or gateway?
[01:50] Priya Patel: Enforcement happens at the routing layer in our control plane. API keys are checked and quota counters updated atomically. For hosted, it's in our multi-tenant control plane; for Dedicated we can either enforce at the Redwood control plane or give you a private shard with a local enforcement proxy. There are tradeoffs for latency vs isolation.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: Quick note — some of the docs call it org-keys and project keys, sometimes project tokens in our older docs. Apologies for the inconsistent lingo.
[02:20] Evan Brooks: On Dedicated vs hosted, our SRE's main ask is network isolation and bringing our own KMS for encryption at rest. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:30] Priya Patel: Yes, Private and Dedicated options support customer KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted we offer BYOK for encryption of customer artifacts in some plans, and we can provide an audited path for keys.
[02:38] Tom Alvarez: Good. Another requirement: we need per-tenant usage reports and an audit trail of admin actions.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: Console has per-token cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and audit logs for key rotations and admin changes. We can export to S3 or forward logs to Splunk.
[02:55] Maya Singh: How are org vs project billing handled? We want to bill tenants internally based on usage.
[03:02] Priya Patel: You can export usage by project, tokens and requests. Many customers run internal chargebacks by project ID. We also support tags on keys for mapping to tenant IDs.
[03:12] Tom Alvarez: On rate-limits: do you support sloped/gradual throttles or only hard caps?
[03:20] Priya Patel: Both — hard caps and adaptive throttling. For bursty tenants you can allow short bursts with a token bucket config; for strict tenants you can set hard RPS and token ceilings.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: We'll show the API too — creating a project key is a simple POST and then you can attach quota policies. Priya, can you run through the API call?
[03:40] Priya Patel: Sure. (typing) POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects with body name and owner, returns project_id and project_key. Then POST /v1/quotas to attach rate limit rules: {type: "tokens_per_minute", limit: 200000} — this is demo data.
[03:58] Maya Singh: Are the keys scoped to specific models or endpoints?
[04:02] Priya Patel: Yes, you can scope to model families (e.g., redwood/gptx-4 or redwood/embedding-v2), or to endpoints like completion vs embedding. That helps with predictable costs.
[04:12] Evan Brooks: Any SDKs to rotate keys automatically? We rotate keys every 30 days.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: We have API endpoints for key rotation and console workflows. You can also integrate with your secrets manager to auto-rotate and pull keys.
[04:25] Tom Alvarez: On throttling behavior — what does the client receive? 429? Backoff header?
[04:30] Priya Patel: 429 with Retry-After header. We also provide X-RateLimit-* headers showing remaining tokens and reset timings. For streaming responses we try to graceful degrade.
[04:42] Tom Alvarez: If a tenant hits their monthly token cap, can we route them to a cheaper model automatically?
[04:47] Priya Patel: Yes, routing policies can send requests to fallback models that are cheaper or to a cached response. You can set per-project fallback policies in the Console. That is one of our Optimize features — automatic downgrade rules.
[05:00] (ambient typing)
[05:10] Jordan Lee: Quick qualification — what's your expected QPS and token mix? That helps us recommend the batch size and quantify cost.
[05:18] Tom Alvarez: Peak requests 250 QPS across tenants, typical prompt+response 700 tokens, embeddings batch calls sporadic.
[05:28] Priya Patel: Okay, so for 250 QPS at 700 tokens, batching can help for embeddings but for completions low latency matters so we'd suggest smaller batch windows. We can show Optimize's recommendations — it looks at request distribution and suggests per-model quantization, batch sizes, and prefetched KV caching for repeated prompts.
[05:45] Maya Singh: In terms of billing windows, do you prorate quotas mid-month?
[05:50] Jordan Lee: Quotas are generally enforced absolutely, but you can set soft thresholds with alerts and allow manual top-ups or auto-increase rules.
[05:58] Evan Brooks: Let's talk about multi-tenant isolation. If one tenant spikes and we have Dedicated, will others be affected?
[06:05] Priya Patel: With Dedicated pools you get reserved compute — tenants still share project pools unless you create separate projects with isolated GPU pools. There is also an option for per-tenant Dedicated shards but that is more expensive. For hosted, we have strict quota enforcement to protect other orgs.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: Also note, prefix/KV caching is per-project — we avoid cross-tenant cache leakage.
[06:27] Tom Alvarez: Can we set SSO and RBAC so only certain product engineers can create project keys?
[06:33] Priya Patel: Yes — org admins set SSO via SAML/Okta, and RBAC roles (admin, billing, dev) control key creation and quota edits.
[06:40] Maya Singh: Good. A few security questions from Evan offline will probably be about key lifecycle and KMS separation.
[06:46] Evan Brooks: Yeah, also data retention windows — how long do you keep request/response logs?
[06:52] Jordan Lee: Configurable. For compliance you can set short retention or disable logging of PII. For Private deployments you can keep logs in your VPC and Redwood doesn't retain them.
[07:05] (brief pause)
[07:10] Priya Patel: Demo: I'm going to create a project and attach a quota quickly — doing so now. (UI clicks) Creating project "claims-summarizer", creating key... showing quota screen, adding rule: 500 requests/minute, 200k tokens/month, concurrency 8. Save. Key generated.
[07:35] Priya Patel: Now run a small script against the API using the project key. (run) Response returned, headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 499, X-RateLimit-Reset: 60.
[07:50] Tom Alvarez: Looks straightforward. If we wanted to temporarily raise a project's quota during a rollout, is there an API to bump it programmatically?
[07:57] Priya Patel: Yes, quota endpoints support PATCH and we also have a rate-limit override API for temporary increases with an expiration timestamp.
[08:06] Maya Singh: For billing accuracy, how soon is usage data available? We need near-real-time for internal billing.
[08:13] Jordan Lee: Usage feeds are near real-time (1-3 minutes) for hosted; dedicated with local proxies can also forward usage to your internal billing systems.
[08:22] Evan Brooks: On logs forwarding, can we get an immutable audit trail?
[08:27] Priya Patel: Yes, we support write-once S3 exports and can deliver signed audit logs.
[08:34] Tom Alvarez: Let's talk edge cases. What happens to in-flight requests when you rotate a key?
[08:40] Jordan Lee: We support key rotation with a grace window where both old and new keys are valid to avoid dropped in-flight requests. You can set the overlap window.
[08:48] (slight crosstalk)
[09:00] Priya Patel: Now switching to Optimize suggestions — this is where Redwood ingests a sample of your traffic and recommends batching, caching TTLs, and potential model quantization to reduce cost while staying within latency SLOs. Example recommendation: for your 700-token typical response, try 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical tasks and set a per-project fallback to that model at 95% of monthly cap.
[09:30] Maya Singh: Is model quantization automatic or do you validate outputs?
[09:34] Priya Patel: We recommend and can run a quality regression test using your prompt set. Rollouts can be canaryed per-project so you can check quality before full switch.
[09:44] Tom Alvarez: On PII — if we flag prompts as PHI, can those bypass logs or be handled differently?
[09:50] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can tag requests with a PII header that instructs Redwood to avoid storing inputs/outputs or to route them to your private deployment.
[09:58] Evan Brooks: Does the PII tag require client changes?
[10:01] Priya Patel: Just add a header X-Redwood-Data-Handling: pii=exclude or route=private. We document this in the API guide.
[10:10] (typing)
[10:20] Jordan Lee: Quick: customers sometimes ask if we support hierarchical quotas (department -> project -> tenant). We do — you can define policy inheritance.
[10:30] Tom Alvarez: Good, our org model will map definitely to that.
[10:35] Maya Singh: For the pilot, we want to test rate limiting behavior at scale. What's the best approach?
[10:41] Priya Patel: Provide sample traffic profile and sample prompts. We'll spin up a sandbox with a Dedicated trial pool and run a benchmark. Priya will run initial latency and token accounting, and then hand over benchmarking artifacts.
[10:55] Jordan Lee: I'll also include a spreadsheet with cost projections under different batching and fallback configs.
[11:03] Evan Brooks: A few follow-ups — can you share SOC 2 report and network diagrams?
[11:08] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll share SOC2, ISO materials and architecture diagrams. We'll also set up a security deep-dive.
[11:15] Tom Alvarez: What's typical SLA for Dedicated?
[11:18] Priya Patel: Dedicated SLA targets 99.9% with latency SLOs documented per model family. We can discuss contract terms with legal once you move past POC.
[11:28] Maya Singh: Any known issues with concurrency limits and streaming? Sometimes streaming connections get torn by proxies.
[11:34] Priya Patel: We tune streaming keepalives and offer connection pooling guidance. For strict proxies we can provide a fallback batch mode.
[11:45] Jordan Lee: Wrapping up — recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing + quotas sheet; Priya send sandbox recording + how-to; Riverbend to provide sample prompts and traffic profile; Evan to compile security questions. We'll schedule the security deep-dive the week of Nov 15.
[11:58] Tom Alvarez: That works. Thanks — demo was helpful and clear.
[12:02] Maya Singh: Thanks both!
[12:05] Evan Brooks: Thank you.
[12:10] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll follow up via email with notes and links.

End of transcript.
